title: Spectroscopy Peak Interactive Viewer with Time Control
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that implements an interactive spectroscopy peak viewer with time-resolved control. The scene simulates an absorption spectrum that evolves over time, representing a chemical reaction where reactant peaks decrease and product peaks increase.

SCENE SETUP:
- Use an orthographic camera looking at a 2D-style spectrum plot rendered in 3D space.
- Background: dark navy (#0a0a2a).
- Create a 3D coordinate system with X-axis representing wavelength (200-800nm), Y-axis representing absorbance (0.0-2.0), and Z-axis representing time depth (visual only).
- Draw axis lines as white LineSegments with tick marks every 100nm on X and every 0.5 on Y.
- Add axis labels using sprite text or canvas textures: 'Wavelength (nm)' on X, 'Absorbance' on Y.

SPECTRUM PEAKS:
- Implement 5 Gaussian peaks as smooth 3D ribbon meshes (ExtrudeGeometry or TubeGeometry along the spectrum curve):
  - Reactant Peak A: center=350nm, sigma=20nm, initial_height=1.8, color=#ff4444
  - Reactant Peak B: center=420nm, sigma=30nm, initial_height=1.2, color=#ff8844
  - Product Peak C: center=550nm, sigma=25nm, initial_height=0.1, color=#44ff44
  - Product Peak D: center=620nm, sigma=15nm, initial_height=0.05, color=#4488ff
  - Isosbestic Point Peak E: center=480nm, sigma=35nm, initial_height=0.7, color=#ffff44 (constant height)

TIME EVOLUTION:
- Time ranges from t=0 to t=100 (arbitrary units).
- Reactant peaks decay exponentially: height(t) = initial_height * exp(-k * t) where k=0.03.
- Product peaks grow: height(t) = max_height * (1 - exp(-k * t)) where max_height for C=1.6, D=1.0.
- Peak E remains constant at 0.7 (isosbestic point verification).
- The total absorbance at 480nm must remain constant (conservation check).

TIME CONTROL:
- Add a DOM slider input (id='time-slider') ranging 0-100 with step 1.
- Add a play/pause button (id='play-btn') that auto-advances time at 1 unit per 100ms.
- Add a speed selector (id='speed-select') with options: 0.5x, 1x, 2x, 4x.
- Add a reset button (id='reset-btn') that sets time back to 0.
- Display current time as text (id='time-display').

INTERACTION:
- Clicking on the 3D spectrum near a peak should highlight that peak (glow effect or thicker line) and show a tooltip (id='peak-tooltip') with peak center wavelength, current height, and FWHM.
- Pressing keys 1-5 selects peaks A-E respectively and highlights them.
- Pressing spacebar toggles play/pause.
- Mouse wheel zooms the orthographic camera in/out on the spectrum.

HUD ELEMENTS:
- A panel (id='info-panel') showing: selected peak name, center wavelength, current absorbance, decay constant.
- A conservation indicator (id='conservation-indicator') that shows green if isosbestic point absorbance is within 0.01 of 0.7, red otherwise.

STATE MANAGEMENT:
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- currentTime: number (0-100)
- isPlaying: boolean
- playbackSpeed: number
- selectedPeakIndex: number or null (0-4)
- peakHeights: array of 5 current peak heights
- peakCenters: [350, 420, 550, 620, 480]
- isosbesticAbsorbance: number (absorbance at 480nm)
- conservationValid: boolean
- cameraZoom: number
- totalAbsorbance: number (sum of all peak heights)
- peakFWHM: array of 5 FWHM values (2.355 * sigma for each)
- reactantSum: number (sum of reactant peak heights)
- productSum: number (sum of product peak heights)

Update __3D_STATE__ every frame.
physics_constraints: Gaussian peak heights must follow exponential kinetics exactly: reactants decay as h*exp(-0.03*t), products grow as hmax*(1-exp(-0.03*t)). Isosbestic point at 480nm must maintain constant absorbance (0.7 ± 0.01). FWHM = 2.355 * sigma for all peaks. Peak heights must never be negative or NaN. Conservation: isosbestic absorbance invariant under time evolution.
